To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
interactive stories are more compelling when they are responsive and engaging, and that the use of unencumbering sensors facilitates immersion in the experience.

1) interactive stories can be designed in such a way that the story path is single, but users can still perceive a strong sense of interactivity, 2) the physical setup and the sensor technology can facilitate immersion in the interactive narrative experience, and 3) the user can be the main character of an interactive story.

physically interactive environments can be used to create compelling interactive narratives, and that the ability to choose between story paths is not necessary for a story to be perceived as interactive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of story environments that are both physically interactive and responsive.
the design of story systems that are both physically interactive and responsive.
the design of interactive story environments in which physical activity and interaction is used to create a sense of responsiveness in the narrative and a sense of immersion in the experience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we are not yet at a point where we can create compelling interactive stories with a single path, but we can create compelling story experiences with multiple paths that can be experienced by many different users.
the physical interactive story environments we have created have been very successful in engaging users in the story and have provided a rich interactive experience.

physically interactive story environments are not just about choice, but about the user's experience of choice and responsiveness in the story environment, and about how this experience is facilitated by the use of unencumbering technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and tested a number of different story systems that have been shown to be engaging and compelling for a variety of audiences and in a variety of contexts.
the combination of a rich narrative structure with physically interactive environments and unencumbering sensor technologies can create a compelling user experience.

we have been exploring how to design interactive narrative story systems that can support the user's physical interaction with a narrative world, and how to make the narrative world itself more physically responsive to the user.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physical environment and the story can be tightly integrated in a way that allows users to interact with characters and objects, and move around the story space.
the physicality of the interaction and the responsiveness of the system can be used to create compelling interactive stories, even when there is a single-path structure to the narrative.
the design of interactive stories can be informed by the design of interactive environments, and that the design of such environments can benefit from a narrative approach.
